items.title: She Planned to Protest Trump. She Didn’t Plan on Getting Punched.
items.author: Jessica Contrera
items.content: <article>Blake Miley yelled “fascist” as President Trump spoke at a midterm campaign rally. The violence that followed “was not right,” she said.</article>

items.title: Netanyahu Is Up for Re-election After Years of War. How Will Voters See Him?
items.author: Isabel Kershner
items.content: <article>The Oct. 7 attacks marred Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s image as Mr. Security. Ahead of elections, he’s trying to sell Israelis on the new, hawkish version of himself.</article>

items.title: Israel Cracks Down in West Bank City After Deadly Attack
items.author: Aaron Boxerman and Fatima AbdulKarim
items.content: <article>Hundreds of Palestinian families fled their homes as the Israeli military raided Hebron. The operation came a day after Palestinian gunmen killed two soldiers.</article>

items.title: The Eyes of Elizabeth Holmes
items.author: Maureen Dowd
items.content: <article>Look into that unblinking gaze and see the abyss.</article>

items.title: 5 Takeaways From Our Investigation of Trump’s Waivers for Polluters
items.author: Maxine Joselow and Eric Lipton
items.content: <article>Chemical plants and other industrial facilities had been required to curb their toxic emissions. A New York Times investigation shows how they got out of it.</article>

items.title: How Trump Gave the Worst Polluters a Free Pass
items.author: Eric Lipton, Maxine Joselow and Mira Rojanasakul
items.content: <article>The president temporarily waived clean-air rules for industrial facilities that spew cancer-causing gases. Then his appointees worked to gut the regulations altogether.</article>

items.title: What Happens if Trump Doesn’t Like the Midterm Results?
items.author: Michelle Cottle, Jamelle Bouie, David French and Derek Arthur
items.content: <article>Hope, dread and the final stretch to Election Day.</article>

items.title: How a Small Student Protest Spread Across France
items.author: Leo Sands
items.content: <article>A movement that began with a few high schools has broadened to encompass labor unions and other activists.</article>

items.title: A 2028 Presidential Poll Finds Vance, Rubio and Several Democrats in the Mix
items.author: Reid J. Epstein and Ruth Igielnik
items.content: <article>The Democratic presidential primary race appears to be wide open, while JD Vance and Marco Rubio led among Republican voters, a New York Times/Siena survey found.</article>

items.title: Why Legal Experts See the Justice Dept.’s Alaska Election Challenge as Dubious
items.author: Charlie Savage
items.content: <article>No obvious legal authority supports a pre-emptive effort to block the certification of Alaska’s Senate election if the Republican incumbent narrowly loses.</article>
